name: Humanitarian funding gap
value: WFP Gaza cuts; Sudan stocks empty
summary: WFP cuts Gaza food aid for 500,000; IOM says its Sudan shelter warehouses are empty
state: WFP cut monthly food aid in Gaza by about 500,000 people from late October because of funding shortfalls (WFP). On 6 Nov UNHCR and IOM said funding lets them reach only about 10% of the 15.4 million people in Sudan who need shelter, and IOM's Sudan warehouses are empty (Reuters via TimesLIVE). No formal suspension of food or health aid in a famine-risk country had been announced as of 6 Nov.
for_you: Mainly affects aid recipients in Gaza and Sudan. Cuts tend to raise malnutrition and push more people to move in search of help.
rubric_hit: Watch: major ration cuts announced (WFP Gaza); no large-scale suspension in famine-risk countries

sources.title: WFP — Funding cuts force WFP to drastically reduce lifesaving assistance in Gaza
TimesLIVE (Reuters) — Millions of displaced Sudanese risk losing shelter as funds run low, UN warns

why: When appeals go unfunded, food aid and health services are cut first; funding gaps lead famine and displacement by months.
drivers: Donor budgets and aid cuts, new crises competing for funds, access constraints.

rubric.alert: Pipeline breaks forcing large-scale suspension of food or health aid in famine-risk countries.
rubric.watch: Funding more than 10 percentage points behind recent years at the same point, or major ration cuts announced.
rubric.normal: UN global appeal funding in line with recent years; no major ration cuts.
